title: Nipah virus research, BSL 4 lab capacity and support for local firms
asked: Mr Gerald Giam asked for the progress of local research into Nipah diagnostic kits and vaccines, whether Singapore has or plans Biosafety Level 4 laboratory capacity to test such vaccines, and what grants or subsidies support local firms doing this research without a commercial market.
response: The main local programme is PREPARE, funded under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise programme, which can involve public-private collaborations. Under it, Duke-NUS, NUS and A*STAR are running six Nipah research projects on diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines, none using live Nipah virus, which would need a BSL 4 lab. Singapore currently has no BSL 4 laboratory for research, and the Ministry of Defence is upgrading DSO National Laboratories to BSL 4. On the supplementary questions, Dr Koh said he has no definitive timelines for research outcomes, that the current Nipah outbreak is localised with no urgency to procure vaccines ahead of time, and that Singapore has stepped up alerts and border monitoring while continuing to share information with regional and global partners.
